decisions.statement: The map is beside the page of the runner stating this property.
The map is written by the landing rather than by an author or by a command.
The map binds an address to the arguments the change takes.
The map reads a change's signature rather than restating that signature.
A runner reads the map as a type rather than as a way to reach a change.
An address the map does not have is refused where that address is written.
A runner naming no page type has no map written for that runner.
A change exporting the run is reached by the map.
A change exporting no run is left out of the map rather than refused.
Whether a change exports the run is read from that change's own code.
The addresses come out sorted rather than in the order the index answers.
Every body the map reads is read through the change rather than off the disk.
A generator that throws leaves a stale map for the typecheck to refuse.
Nothing the map holds survives into the code that runs.

definition: the type binding each change address to that change's own arguments
